summary: Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Oxford (~1879–1884) under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1906) and President of Otani University (~1914–1923).

Bunzaburo Matsumoto worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893), where he later held a post (~1899–1906), before serving at Kyoto University from 1906 to 1929 and as professor (attested 1934).

Burkhard Quessel is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997. He later served as a curator at the British Library, attested from 2002 to 2012.

Burton Watson specialized in Sinology and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University (~1946–1956), and held posts at Kyoto University (~1952–1960), Stanford University (~1960–1961), and Columbia University (~1961–1973), where he served as Professor.

Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery under Thubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam, and later taught Jigme Phuntsok, Tarthang Tulku, Khenpo Chökhyap, and Khenpo Dazer.

C. D. Sebastian specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Abhimanyu Singh, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, Paul Williams, and Gavin D'Costa, and was Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. F. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1970) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972), later serving as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong (1994–2015).

C. Kunhan Raja was an Indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1927 and 1946. His students included K. Kunjunni Raja, Madhav Krishna Sharma, and H. G. Narahari.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his F.A. studies at Madras Christian College and earned his university degree from Pachaiyappa's College.
C. S. Srinivasachariar worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and as a professor at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an Indologist who held a post at The Madras Sanskrit College and served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1951. He taught Tomy Augustine.

C. W. Huntington worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency University, Kolkata (~1928–1932) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri, and held posts at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935–1946), Indian Museum (1946), and National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

Calvert Watkins was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (~1950–1959), where he subsequently held an academic post from 1959 to 2003, before serving at the University of California, Los Angeles from 2003 to 2013.

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University, Florida State University, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), guided by advisors including Richard F. Nance, Bryan J. Cuevas, and doctoral supervisor Ulrike Roesler.

Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu, earned a PhD from Harvard University, and held academic posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.

Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas, with Joseph Hellweg serving on his committee.

Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at Cambridge (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS University of London, and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Libraries (attested 2019).

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and completed his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1970–1980). He served on the editorial board at Stanford University (~1980–2013) and was a member of the Numata Center (attested 2017).

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, as well as Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD), and Jena (Habilitation). In 1875, he became a professor at the University of Jena.
